title: Extracting compositions from Seurat and anndata metadata
text: Seurat object, ExtractClusterComposition() reads requested columns meta.data, aggregates cells subjects, returns composition object. Expression counts irrelevant enrichment step; metadata mapping matters. example creates minimal object extraction path can run without study-sized dataset.
code: library(HellingerDistanceEnrichment)  if (requireNamespace("Seurat", quietly = TRUE)) {   n_cells <- 120   meta <- data.frame(     subjectId = rep(paste0("Donor", 1:6), each = 20),     category = sample(paste0("Cluster", 0:3), n_cells, replace = TRUE),     group = rep(c("Control", "Control", "Control", "Case", "Case", "Case"), each = 20),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   )    counts <- matrix(     stats::rpois(100 * n_cells, lambda = 2),     nrow = 100,     ncol = n_cells   )   colnames(counts) <- paste0("cell", seq_len(n_cells))   rownames(counts) <- paste0("gene", seq_len(100))    seu <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(counts = counts, meta.data = meta)    composition <- ExtractClusterComposition(     seu,     subjectCol = "subjectId",     categoryCol = "category",     groupCol = "group"   )    print(composition)    result <- CompareGroupCompositions(     composition,     method = "permutation",     nPermutations = 50,     seed = 1   )   result$omnibus } else {   message("Seurat not installed; skipping Seurat example.") } #> Warning: Data is of class matrix. Coercing to dgCMatrix. #> CategoryComposition with 6 subjects, 4 categories, and 2 groups #> $effectSize #> [1] 0.9485571 #>  #> $pValue #> [1] 0.4705882

HPC deployments, bind-mount study metadata runtime rather baking cohort files container images; extraction step remains portable across environments cohort annotations stay outside image layer.
code: if (requireNamespace("anndata", quietly = TRUE)) {   obs <- data.frame(     subjectId = rep(paste0("S", 1:4), each = 15),     category = sample(paste0("Type", 0:2), 60, replace = TRUE),     group = rep(c("A", "A", "B", "B"), each = 15),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   )   X <- matrix(stats::rnorm(60 * 10), nrow = 60)   adata <- anndata::AnnData(X = X, obs = obs)    composition <- ExtractClusterComposition(     adata,     subjectCol = "subjectId",     categoryCol = "category",     groupCol = "group"   )    CompareGroupCompositions(     composition,     nPermutations = 30,     seed = 2   )$omnibus } else {   message("anndata not installed; skipping anndata example.") } #> $effectSize #> [1] 0.997142 #>  #> $pValue #> [1] 1

title: Hellinger enrichment on synthetic compositions
text: permutation panel marks significance label-shuffle null. Bayes panel shows posterior-mean effect sizes 95% intervals, composition uncertainty group-label uncertainty appear display. Permutation contrast panel omnibus reference. Bayesian posterior-mean contrasts 95% intervals. two methods therefore answer related non-equivalent questions. Plain permutation asks whether group labels exchangeable given fixed composition estimates. posterior-predictive Bayes path nests composition uncertainty inside label null, plain permutation test account . category counts sparse, nesting can change contrasts appear stable. synthetic enrichment used strong enough paths recover planted structure; real cohorts often require Bayes path decide whether apparent contrast survives sampling variation compositions .

title: HellingerDistanceEnrichment
text: Permutation: shuffle group labels; p-value includes observed ratio (workbook style). Bayes: Dirichlet posterior draw subject compositions, run full nested permutation null; report posterior mean p-value effect-size credible intervals. Effect size mean -group pairwise Hellinger distance divided mean within-group pairwise distance. Contrast p-values Holm-adjusted default; omnibus statistic unadjusted.
